records.name: Walnut Hill Community Association
records.summary: Residents of Walnut Hill who work on neighborhood improvements, local events, and support for neighbors. Committees look after a playground on Sansom Street and the Max Paul Farm on Market Street.
records.what_you_do: Fill in the membership form and pay dues to join, or come to the community meeting first. Members take part in the committees for the playground and the farm.

schedule.text: Community meeting on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Regular meeting days and times are not published.

cost.text: Individual membership is $20 a year. Youth is $5, family $30, and business $50. Dues run January 1 to December 31.

first_step.how: Fill in the membership form on the group's join page and pay dues by PayPal, cash or check. Or come to the community meeting on October 29, 2026 first.
first_step.basis: The community meeting is announced publicly and the join form is public, but full membership needs annual dues of $20 for an individual.

records.notes: The news items carry no publication dates. The only dated items are 2026 events: a Penn Family Frisbee Festival on Saturday, October 17, 2026, and the community meeting on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Footer copyright not used as evidence. Neighborhood bounds per the site: Market Street, 45th Street, Spruce Street and 52nd Street. The join page also takes a mailed check made out to the group, sent to the treasurer at 4635 Locust Street, Philadelphia, PA 19139. The phone line reaches a board member on weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm and takes messages. The committees page was linked but not read.

records.name: Mill Creek Urban Farm
records.summary: A farm on Brown Street in West Philadelphia that grows produce without chemicals and teaches farm classes for all ages. It also runs a farmers market.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on the farm through the volunteer form (wear a hat and protective boots), help at the market, or ask about a group visit.

schedule.text: Farmers market on Saturdays from noon to 2 pm at 49th and Brown streets. The same page also says the market is coming soon, so confirm before going. Volunteer days are not published.

cost.text: Prices are not listed. The market accepts FMNP vouchers.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the farm's site, email millcreekfarmphilly@gmail.com, or visit the Saturday market.
first_step.basis: The market is open to visitors, and the site lists a volunteer form and an email address.

records.notes: The site shows no dated events and no year. It says 'Farmers Market Coming Soon!' while also giving Saturday market hours, so confirm the market before a visitor relies on it. The mailing address is a PO box in 19151. The farm is a program of A LittleTaste of Everything, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit.

records.name: Overbrook Farms Club
records.summary: The civic club for the Overbrook Farms neighborhood. Members must own or long-term rent a home in the club's area, and they attend board and community meetings and take part in events such as History Night.
records.what_you_do: Apply to become a member, then take part in board and community meetings and neighborhood events.

schedule.text: Board meetings and community meetings are held. Dates and times are not published. Membership renews each January.

cost.text: No dues or application fee is published.

first_step.how: Complete the membership form on the club's site. The membership committee checks your address, and the board adds you at its next meeting. Use the contact form for questions.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application, an address check and a board vote before you are an official member.

records.notes: Eligibility: 18 or older, and owns or is a long-term tenant of property in the 58th to 66th Street, City Avenue to Woodbine Avenue area (plus the 6400 and 6600 blocks of Woodcrest Avenue and Morris Park Road). Membership is per person and renews by confirming details each January. The page does not say whether non-members can attend meetings or events. History Night 2026 is listed with no date. Copyright footer not used as evidence. No phone or email is published; use the contact form. A 2019 article gives a founding year of 1892 and links a second domain, overbrookfarmsclub.org, which returned a certificate error when checked. Not confirmed as the same group.

notes: Slice is thin on checkable groups with their own websites, and the search budget ran out (6 of 6 used). Three records written. Dropped with reasons: Cathedral Park CDC (broad area 'West Philadelphia', programs listed with no schedules, no way to join or volunteer), Calvary Center for Culture and Community (a community space with no address, contact details or dated content; looks like a venue, so likely not_a_group), Carroll Park Community Council (a 2012 search snippet says it closed for lack of funding; source not read, so not published as defunct). Could not read: the city's April 2026 registered community organization PDF (the fetch returned only link annotations), and the park friends list (an interactive map with no text). Domains that did not resolve on 2026-10-08: noah19151.com and opca19151.org. A TLS certificate error on overbrookfarmsclub.org. Search summaries disagreed on Council district lines (one said Haddington and Overbrook sit in District 4; West Philly neighborhoods sit in District 3); I did not verify district boundaries. Business associations (Lancaster Avenue, City Avenue, Haverford Avenue, Lansdowne Avenue) were not recorded because they are not community programs. Mill Creek and Dunlap search found no current civic association; Dunlap was not checked further. Walnut Hill's membership is the only paid join path found in this slice; the other records are free or unknown.
